threads.title: First real upgrade from AirPods: Blessing 3 or EW300?
threads.body:
Budget is around $300. Mostly lo-fi, city pop and some metal on the commute (BTS, so it's loud). Phone is a Pixel with USB-C.

Sotto says both are fine straight from the Apple dongle, so I don't need an amp yet, right? What would you pick and why?

comments.body:
For metal on a train I'd lean Blessing 3, the bass is tighter and it isolates better. EW300 is more fun and warmer, but it's chunkier in the ear.

And yes, the dongle is fine for both. They're easy to drive.
Fit is a good point, I have small ears. Is the B3 shell big?
Medium-ish. Try a smaller tip before you decide it doesn't fit, it makes a huge difference.
Checked both in Build with the Apple adapter: both say "loud enough" with headroom. If you ever add a dongle with a high gain switch, keep it on low with IEMs like these.

Same experience here. The Apple dongle is great for IEMs, but the HD600 wants a bit more voltage on peaks. A desktop amp is nice, not required.

threads.title: My small desk setup after 2 years: DX3 Pro + Sundara
threads.body:
Nothing fancy, but I finally stopped upgrading.

- Source: PC over USB
- DAC/amp: Topping DX3 Pro
- Headphones: HiFiMAN Sundara (pads swapped once)

Sotto puts the Sundara well under the DX3 Pro's line on the chart, so it drives it with room to spare. Happy to answer questions.

Ran it off a laptop jack for a week before this. It played, but turned up loud it fell apart on busy tracks. The DX3 Pro fixed that.

threads.title: 10.10: the Real price page matched my checkout to the baht
threads.body:
Had a ฿16,490 amp in the cart, a 20% shop code and the app offered a 25% platform code capped at ฿6,000.

Put the same numbers into Real price before paying: it said ฿9,894. Checkout said ฿9,894. Also it told me the 30% code I was about to use was worse because its cap was lower.

Tip: collect every code first, then let the page compare the pairs.

comments.body: The cap thing gets everyone. A bigger % with a low cap loses on anything expensive.

threads.title: Hiss with sensitive IEMs on a KA17, solved (it was the gain)
threads.body:
Got background hiss in quiet tracks with my multi-BA IEMs on the KA17. Thought something was broken.

Turned out I'd left it on high gain from using it with headphones. Low gain and the hiss is basically gone. This is what Sotto means by "more than enough": a very sensitive IEM on a strong source.

Posting in case someone else panics like I did.

comments.body: Classic. An impedance adapter is the other fix if low gain still isn't quiet enough, but it can change the sound on multi-driver IEMs.
ขอบคุณครับ เกือบส่งเคลมไปแล้ว ลองปรับ gain ตามนี้หายเลย

threads.title: Finally a proper desktop DAC/amp: FiiO K9 [first impressions]
threads.body:
Upgraded from a dongle last month. Quick notes, no fancy review.

**Pros:**

- Every input I need: USB, optical, coax, line in, Bluetooth
- 6.35, 4.4 and XLR4 out on the front
- Low/mid/high gain switch, so IEMs and harder headphones both work

**Cons:**

- Big. Takes more desk than I expected
- The antenna sticks up and looks a bit silly

**Disclaimer:** bought with my own money.

Build puts my HD650 well inside what it can drive. Sotto lists this one without power specs yet, so I checked with the K9 Pro numbers instead.

*Photo: Benlisquare, CC BY-SA 4.0, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:FiiO_K9.jpg)*

comments.body: that knob is chef's kiss
Use low gain with IEMs on this thing. Ask me how I know.
already learned that one the loud way 💀
ซื้อที่ไหนครับ ร้านไทยหรือสั่งนอก
ร้านไทยครับ ช่วงโปรเดือนก่อน ใส่โค้ดร้าน + โค้ดแพลตฟอร์ม เช็คในหน้าราคาจริงก่อนจ่าย

threads.title: Weekend project: built a Bottlehead Crack (DIY tube amp)
threads.body:
Two weekends, one burnt fingertip, zero regrets. Running it with my high-impedance Sennheisers, which is what OTL tube amps like this are known for.

Not something Sotto can calculate (kit, no store listing), just sharing because it's pretty.

*Photo: John Donovan, CC BY 3.0, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bottlehead_Crack_Headphone_Amplifier_(116368567).jpg)*

comments.body: the wood box is so clean. what finish?
just oil, two coats. the top plate is spray paint
Can't wait for the day I'm brave enough to solder mains voltage. Not today.
Heads up for anyone tempted: OTL tube amps like this suit high-impedance cans. Low-impedance planars and IEMs are a bad match.

threads.title: DT 770 Pro 250 ohm straight from a laptop?
threads.body:
Got these for editing at uni. They play from my laptop jack but I'm at like 90% volume. Normal or do I need something?

*Photo: Alex Holyoake, CC0, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Top_view_of_headphones_hanging_from_a_desk_(Unsplash).jpg)*

comments.body: Normal for the 250 ohm version. It needs more voltage than a laptop jack usually gives. A small dongle with more output fixes it, you don't need a big amp.
Pick one in Build and compare it against your laptop. If the bar goes green you're done.
